Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the time. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so your security and procurement teams have what they need: 

What we covered (recap)
- Types of data we saw in the demo: user prompts and model outputs (potentially PII depending on your product flows).
- Data retention: configurable retention windows for request logs and audit logs; ability to purge on demand for private deployments.
- Logging controls: token-level telemetry, structured request metadata, and audit trails that can be exported to SIEM.
- Encryption: in-transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at-rest (AES-256) by default.
- Customer-managed keys (CMEK/BYOK) and HSM options for private deployments.

Open items / clarifying questions from your side
- Confirmed requirement: do you need customer-managed keys for all persisted data (models, logs, backups), or only for primary model artifacts and backups?
- Any constraints around HSM (FIPS 140-2/3) or specific cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault)?
- Retention policy target (we heard ~90 days for request logs) and whether export of raw logs to your SIEM is required.

Next steps
1) Attaching our KMS options doc (redwood-kms-options.pdf) and a high-level architecture diagram.
2) Dev (cc'd) will follow up with the technical KMS/HSM details and how envelope encryption is implemented.
3) If helpful, we can set a short security-only call next week to align on procurement requirements and any SOC2 evidence needs.

If you can confirm the answers to the three open items above, we'll put together a brief Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a preliminary SOW for procurement.

Thanks for the clear recap and the doc. A few answers and follow-ups from our side: 

1) CMEK scope: We need customer-managed keys for all persisted data related to production requests — that includes model checkpoints/backups and request logs. We can discuss if cache/prefixing needs the same level, but for baseline treat everything as CMEK-required.
2) HSM/FIPS: We require FIPS 140-2 compliance for any HSM-based key material. Primary preference is AWS KMS with CloudHSM, but we may also need GCP KMS compatibility depending on region strategy.
3) Retention: 90 days for request logs is accurate. We will want automated export to our Splunk instance (SaaS) and an option to redact PII before export if possible.

Hi Jane / Samir —

Thanks — wanted to surface concrete answers to the technical questions so you can take them to procurement/security: 

Encryption (in-transit & at-rest)
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 enforced for all customer traffic; TLS 1.2 allowed for legacy clients by exception.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM for data at rest. Keys are managed via a hierarchy (envelope encryption) so we never expose raw data key material.

Customer-managed keys (CMEK / BYOK)
- Hosted (Redwood-managed control plane): we support customer-managed keys via integration with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault (customer provides key policy and we call KMS for envelope encryption operations).
- Dedicated / Private deployments: full BYOK/HSM option — you can bring keys into a Cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM) or an on-prem HSM (PKCS#11 supported). FIPS 140-2/3 modules supported for private deployments.
- Key rotation: automated rotation via KMS for data keys; master key rotation follows provider policies. We support re-encryption workflows for snapshots/backups upon rotation for dedicated/private deployments (re-encryption for hosted workloads is done via envelope keys with rotation but long-term snapshot re-encryptions can be coordinated).

Logging & Audit
- Key usage logs: we surface KMS audit events (decrypt/encrypt calls) in our audit logs; for hosted customers, we provide a 90-day retention default with export hooks to your SIEM. For Dedicated/Private, retention is customer-configurable and logs can be routed to your logging endpoint (Splunk, Datadog, S3).
- No plaintext of customer request/response material is written to logs. Redaction: we offer PII redaction hooks pre-export (configurable regex/structured rules).

Operational impact
- Latency: CMEK adds a small crypto call (envelope key unwrap) at write time — typical p99 increase ~5-20ms depending on region and KMS provider. For read/serve paths we cache decrypted data keys in-memory for short-lived tasks to avoid repeated unwrap calls.
- Cost: KMS API call costs apply for hosted CMEK usage (per-decrypt/per-encrypt) — we can provide a cost estimate based on expected request volume. Dedicated/private pricing can include a fixed fee for HSM support.

Attachments included: redwood-kms-arch-diagram.png (high-level architecture), soc2-extract-2026.pdf (SOC2 excerpts relevant to encryption). Also attached the redwood-kms-options.pdf Marissa sent.
